chosen.premise: Farmers plant trees Diglett likes to eat, luring it into plowing the fields around their crops.
chosen.hook: Farmers bait Diglett with the trees it likes to eat.
chosen.visualIdea: Show farmers planting a preferred tree, then Diglett following its roots and leaving a freshly plowed field.
chosen.note: The strangest and most Diglett-specific premise: farmers deliberately plant trees it eats to make it plow fields. It is directly supported by one entry, with related root-eating evidence elsewhere.

candidates.premise: Diglett can prepare perfect farmland, yet its root-chewing makes it a pest around vulnerable crops.
candidates.hook: Diglett is both a farmer’s helper and their crop problem.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen: one Diglett tills tidy soil while another chews roots and damages a crop.
candidates.note: A clear contradiction with excellent split-screen potential; the two-sided farming relationship is well supported.

candidates.premise: Alolan Diglett keeps the same height but gains Steel typing and weighs 0.2 kilograms more.
candidates.hook: Alolan Diglett changes type and weight without changing height.
candidates.visualIdea: Morph standard Diglett into Alolan Diglett, keeping a 0.2-meter height bar while adding Steel and shifting weight from 0.8 to 1 kilogram.
candidates.note: A precise, fully supported comparison with strong graphics, but it is more of a stats transformation than a compelling behavioral story.

candidates.premise: Farmers raise Diglett because every tunnel leaves soil perfectly tilled for growing crops.
candidates.hook: Some farmers don’t buy a plow—they raise Diglett.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Diglett burrowing beneath a field, with neat tilled rows appearing behind it and vegetables growing.
candidates.note: Strongly documented and easy to visualize, but the basic farming-helper premise is less unusual than the baiting detail.

candidates.premise: Diglett’s thin skin makes bright light dangerous: its blood heats up and it grows weak.
candidates.hook: Diglett doesn’t just hate sunlight—it physically weakens it.
candidates.visualIdea: Cut from Diglett underground to a bright sunbeam, then show a heat meter rising as Diglett wilts.
candidates.note: A concrete biological weakness supported directly by the Gold entry, though the broader sunlight-aversion angle is already familiar.

candidates.premise: Diglett lives about one yard underground, surfacing only occasionally or when the sun is no longer bright.
candidates.hook: Diglett’s normal home is one yard beneath your feet.
candidates.visualIdea: Use a cutaway field showing Diglett at one-yard depth, then follow its raised-earth trail to the surface.
candidates.note: The one-yard measurement is concrete, but the depth is not especially surprising and the surfacing behavior varies across entries.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required. A future refinement could add a second source confirming the farming tactic, but the existing Ultra Moon entry directly supports the premise.
